stem: One irrigation event applies much more water than the root zone can retain, producing substantial drainage. What is the most useful interpretation?
choices: Applied volume and retained root-zone water are different quantities, so drainage and moisture response should be evaluated
All applied water remains available to roots
The event automatically improves aeration indefinitely
rationale: Not all delivered water is retained in the root zone. Drainage and post-irrigation moisture help distinguish applied volume from actual stored water.
